chapter: Alfred Williams and the Ruidoso summer
title: Ruidoso summer, the white band from Dallas, and the band visiting Watts's dance
summary: Alfred tells of playing for a white resort crowd who treated the Black band royally, and of going to Watts's dance in Central, where Watts played all the Louis Armstrong records.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Wasn't that, ain't that the time when I would bat up in Central? When y'all used to come over and visit us on Sunday when we was off? You remember when I was playing with Bat Brown at Suckoff's place? He used to play at Lewis. In Central, Lewis Suckoff.

No, but we was playing, we was playing for Miss Swutchikon then. Oh. What's her name? We used to play with Mel then. I was playing with Melvin then. Oh. I was in 37. Oh, oh. And rolling at 11. But this is later when you played near us in Central. I was in Central there. Oh yeah, in 37. Yeah. You see that was June of 36 in Rio Dosa. Uh-uh. And man, that boy had a fine band. We'd go up there and listen to them. The voice, he had seven pieces. Uh-huh. And we couldn't play with about four or five numbers. Dino, Sweet Sue, and Kellis, and Lowe. Yeah. And Graham, Graham something was his name out of Dallas. Mm-hmm. A fine band. Mm-hmm. And you know we used to close them people up every Saturday night. And we just put those on. And that boy had a fine band, boy. Yeah. I'm telling you. But that ain't what they wanted. No. They wanted us. Yeah. Seeing the Negroes. Yeah. Yeah. And they were so surprised the people down in Texas. Yeah. And they had maids with them, you know, with the baby. Oh yeah. And we got straight then when the maids were there. Oh yeah. They'd come stay two weeks, you know. Uh-huh. Then another gang would come stay two weeks. Yeah. But they had but five, six of us there. Uh-huh. The colored people, the band and the shoot shot. Yeah. Yeah. But they treat us royal. They really are. They didn't want nobody to insult us and say, no. Nothing. They're worried our feelings. No. We played there all the summer. And that's why we went to Roswell. And you just, you was to play a dance. We played one of your dances. Yes you did. At the Umry. Yeah. Something we all called broke down or something. Yeah. On a Thursday night. That was the first night off. Yeah. That was the night they had the dances. Yeah. And they said, look, why little Louis? Yeah. So I said, why little Louis? Yeah. Yeah. Well, Delvin Wright, you know, with us. Yeah. Lacey, Russell. Well, they did. Lacey, they knew you from down east Texas. Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. You see that going down there. Yeah. Yeah. I said that. He said he from New Orleans, Alfred. You ought to know him. I said, Bob, why sure I know him. He said, man, he out there raising the hell all out there with that little Louis. Man, play all the Louis records. I tell you. I said, what? Not bragging. I can't hear it so much for the trumpet that's concerned. Boy, listen. I was collecting scalps.
Boy, listen. People was around that dance like that. Yes, indeed. I'm telling, waiting for y'all. Yeah. So we five come from Rio Dosa, the boss left us off that Thursday night.
I said, I'll be y'all going to take the car. We didn't have no car for transportation. Yeah.
He said, I'll put the car in your hands.

Willie Walker. Yeah. Oh, yeah. So he say, I said, all right. He said, now, I want y'all to listen to Alfred with that automobile. I put in his gear but I couldn't drive, you see. But Willie was pretty good. He was all right. Yeah. He listened to me. He got drunk and said, put the car somewhere. Yeah. We had trumpet, drum, sax, guitar. Drum, alto, sax, guitar, and piano.
Yeah, I know what you're speaking about. I can't call that name, though. And man, that's nice, man.

But we ain't know but six numbers. That's all we knew. That's all they knew, you know? And we go over and over, and you couldn't get in Mr. Clayton's place. Couldn't get in there. And them boys would be coming down there, sitting down there looking at us playing about 10 o'clock. And them boys had a wonderful band. We'd go down there to their rehearsal. None of our band could read, you know? We were just listening. Wonderful band. But you tried to- But he said they got there. The man said, well, I said, I wish I could have had y'all. Say the band cost too much money. See, they couldn't keep them, you see? They had to leave. But there were some very nice boys.
